Who were the first people in space?

And which spaceships did they fly in?

A journey through time – from 1957 until today

Audience: 4th grade. Start by asking "Who do you think was first?" Use arrow keys or the clicker to move on; "i" shows the picture source.

1957The first satellite: Sputnik 1

No people on board yet: this metal ball was the first satellite to circle the Earth, beeping as it went.
Things moved fast after that.

Image source

Sputnik 1 – NASA/NSSDC (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain (NASA)

Open original page ↗

Mention: a few weeks later the dog Laika flew on Sputnik 2 – the first animal in orbit.

12 April 1961Yuri Gagarin – the first human in space

Spaceship: Vostok 1 – a ball just over 2 metres wide.
The 27-year-old Russian flew once around the whole Earth – in just 108 minutes! Shortly before landing he jumped out and came down by parachute.

Image source

Soviet Union stamps for Gagarin's flight, 1961 (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain

Open original page ↗

5 May 1961Alan Shepard – the first American in space

Spaceship: Mercury "Freedom 7".
The flight lasted only 15 minutes: up into space and straight back down, without circling the Earth.

Image source

Launch of "Freedom 7" – NASA (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain (NASA)

Open original page ↗

20 February 1962John Glenn – the first American in orbit

Spaceship: Mercury "Friendship 7".
Glenn circled the Earth three times – in just under five hours.

Image source

John Glenn entering "Friendship 7" – NASA (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain (NASA)

Open original page ↗

16 June 1963Valentina Tereshkova – the first woman in space

Spaceship: Vostok 6.
She was 26 years old and stayed in space for almost three days – 48 laps around the Earth!

Image source

Soviet Union stamp, 1963 (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain

Open original page ↗

18 March 1965Alexei Leonov – the first spacewalk

Spaceship: Voskhod 2.
Leonov floated freely in space for about 12 minutes. His suit puffed up like a balloon – he had to let air out so he could fit back inside!

Image source

Soviet Union stamp, 1965 (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain

Open original page ↗

July 1969Apollo 11 – the first people on the Moon

The giant Saturn V rocket carried Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins to the Moon.
Armstrong and Aldrin landed in the lunar module "Eagle". Look in Buzz's visor: that's Neil taking the photo!

Image source

Buzz Aldrin on the Moon (photographed by Neil Armstrong), Apollo 11 – NASA (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain (NASA)

Open original page ↗

26 August 1978Sigmund Jähn – the first German in space

Spaceship: Soyuz 31.
Together with Valery Bykovsky he flew to the space station "Salyut 6" and stayed in space for about a week.

Image source

Soviet Union stamp, 1978: Soyuz 31 at Salyut 6 (Wikimedia Commons)

License: Public domain

Open original page ↗

15 October 2003Yang Liwei – the first Chinese in space

Spaceship: Shenzhou 5 ("Divine Vessel").
After Russia and the USA, China became the third country to send people into space with its own rocket.

Image source

Shenzhou 5 return capsule and Yang Liwei's spacesuit (National Museum of China) – Gary Lee Todd (Wikimedia Commons)

License: CC0 (Public Domain Dedication)

todayAnd today? The space station ISS

Since the year 2000, people have always been living on the ISS, about 400 km above us. It circles the Earth every 90 minutes.
In the photo, the "Crew Dragon" spaceship is flying up to the ISS.

Any questions?

Image source

Crew Dragon "Endeavour" approaching the ISS – NASA (Wikimedia Commons)
